request.spec:
Selected claims can be moved to another person together: a select of the person and a button
beside the bulk buttons. Each selected claim is moved in list order by exactly the rules of moving
one claim (who may, which statuses, closed periods, retirement, with the same CLAIM_REASSIGNED and
rollup lines); each that cannot is left as it is. Show how many were moved and how many were
refused.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Selected claims can be moved to another person together: a select of the person and a button
beside the bulk buttons. Each selected claim is moved in list order by exactly the rules of moving
one claim (who may, which statuses, closed periods, retirement, with the same CLAIM_REASSIGNED and
rollup lines); each that cannot is left as it is. Show how many were moved and how many were
refused.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added the bulk move: a person select (`bulk-reassign-to`) and a button (`bulk-reassign`) beside the bulk Open and Settle buttons. When it finishes it shows how many claims were moved (`bulk-reassigned`) and how many were refused (`bulk-reassign-refused`). All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works:** the new file `src/main/frontend/features/claims/bulkreassign.slot.tsx` is built the same way as bulk-settle. It goes through the selected claims in list order (people as listed, newest claim first) and sends each one to the existing single-move endpoint. That means each claim gets the same permission, status and closed-period checks, and the same `CLAIM_REASSIGNED` and rollup audit lines, as moving it by hand. A refused claim is left as it is. The counts clear when the button is pressed again, and the selection is cleared once it's done.

**Two changes to moving a single claim**, in `ApplyReassign.java`, because the test needs them:
- **Retirement check added.** Moving one claim never checked retirement, though the request names it as a rule. Now a claim dated after the new person's retirement date is refused. It uses the same check as adding or re-dating a claim, so a claim dated on the retirement date itself is still allowed.
- **"Already this person's" refusal removed.** The test expects moving Ben's claim to Ben to succeed and be audited `from=Ben to=Ben`. The single Move select never lists the claim's own person, so on screen nothing changes there. A direct call to the endpoint can now "move" a claim to its own person, which puts it at the top of that person's list and drops any figure a statement had fixed on it.
